rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Abu Abd Allah says believers entering Paradise may be spouses; God lets the higher-ranked spouse choose, and if the lower-ranked one is better, lets that spouse choose.
rows.anchor: عن أبي بصير عن أبي عبد الله ع قال: قلت له جعلت فداك أخبرني عن الرجل المؤمن

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Paradise has multiple gardens and ranks, with people distinguished by their deeds.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبد الله ع: لا تقولن الجنة واحدة إن الله يقول ومن دونهما جنتان

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Those in higher stations may descend to visit lower-ranked believers; lower-ranked believers cannot ascend, but loved ones meet on couches when they wish.
rows.anchor: إن المؤمنين يدخلان الجنة فيكون أحدهما أرفع مكانا من الآخر فيشتهي أن يلقى صاحبه

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Abu Abd Allah rejects placing people released from Hell among God's close friends: they were neither unbelievers, who cannot enter Paradise, nor believers, who would not enter Hell.
rows.anchor: عن العلاء بن سيابة عن أبي عبد الله ع قال: قلت له إن الناس يتعجبون منا إذا قلنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the report is sound, those people were not among the most excellent and best of the believers.
rows.anchor: وتأويل هذا لو صح الخبر أنهم لم يكونوا من أفاضل المؤمنين وأخيارهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two gardens are deep green, darkened by abundant moisture; full green tends toward black, its most beautiful state.
rows.anchor: أي من خضرتهما قد اسودتا من الري وكل نبت أخضر فتمام خضرته أن يضرب إلى السواد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas takes the four gardens as all belonging to those who fear their Lord's station.
rows.anchor: وهذا على قول من قال إن الجنات الأربع لمن خاف مقام ربه وهو قول ابن عباس

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan assigns the first two gardens to the forerunners and the latter two to their followers.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الأوليان للسابقين والأخريان للتابعين عن الحسن

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan explains the two fountains as gushing water that rises from its source and then flows.
rows.anchor: أي فوارتان بالماء ينبع من أصلهما ثم يجريان عن الحسن

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the fountains spray musk, ambergris, and camphor upon God's friends.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس تنضخ على أولياء الله بالمسك والعنبر والكافور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says that when three people are together, two should not whisper apart from the third, since this grieves the excluded person.
rows.anchor: إذا كنتم ثلاثة فلا يتناج اثنان دون صاحبهما فإن ذلك يحزنه

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn Umar transmits the instruction that two people should not whisper privately while leaving the third out.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عمر عنه قال: لا يتناج اثنان دون الثالث

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: On the day of Banu Nadir, the Prophet offered the Ansar a choice: share homes and property with the emigrants and share the booty, or keep their property and receive none of it.
rows.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يوم بني النضير للأنصار

rows.speaker: الأنصار
rows.claim: The Ansar chose to share their wealth and homes and give the emigrants all the booty without taking a share themselves; the verse was revealed about this.
rows.anchor: فقال الأنصار: بل نقسم لهم من أموالنا وديارنا ونؤثرهم بالغنيمة ولا نشاركهم فيها فنزلت

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One reported occasion is seven thirsty men at Uhud who passed a cup of water along; all died without drinking, and God praised them.
rows.anchor: وقيل: نزلت في سبعة عطشوا في يوم أحد فجيء بماء يكفي لأحدهم فقال واحد منهم ناول فلانا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another occasion is an Ansari who hosted a hungry visitor of the Prophet, serving the children's food while the couple pretended to eat and went to bed hungry; the Prophet recited this verse in the morning.
rows.anchor: وقيل: نزلت في رجل جاء إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: أطعمني فإني جائع فبعث إلى أهله

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: In the account with a sound chain from Abu Hurayra, the host who hid the lack of food and put out the lamp was Ali and Fatima.
rows.anchor: وأما الذي رويناه بإسناد صحيح عن أبي هريرة أن الذي أضافه ونوم الصبية وأطفأ السراج علي ع وفاطمة ع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The property restored to the Prophet was taken from the Jews of Banu Nadir whom he expelled; the ruling extends to disbelievers subject to the same status.
rows.anchor: أي من اليهود الذين أجلاهم وإن كان الحكم ساريا في جميع الكفار الذين حكمهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ijaf is the urging on of mounts, below the degree of taqrib; the Muslims did not hasten to Banu Nadir on horses or camels, but walked there from nearby Medina.
rows.anchor: والإيجاف دون التقريب. وقيل: الإيجاف

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One lexical view reserves ijaf for horses and ida for camels.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الإيجاف في الخيل والإيضاع في الإبل

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view uses both ijaf and ida for either horses or camels.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هما مستعملان فيهما جميعا أي فما أوجفتم عليه خيلا ولا إبلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rikab means camels that carry a group of people; its singular is rahila.
rows.anchor: والركاب الإبل التي تحمل القوم واحدتها راحلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gives His messengers power over an enemy without fighting by casting terror into their hearts.
rows.anchor: أي يمكنهم من عدوهم من غير قتال بأن يقذف الرعب في قلوبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made Banu Nadir's property exclusive to the Prophet, who distributed it among the emigrants, except for three needy Ansar: Abu Dujana, Sahl ibn Hunayf, and al-Harith ibn al-Simma.
rows.anchor: فقسمها رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بين المهاجرين ولم يعط الأنصار منها شيئا إلا ثلاثة نفر كانت بهم حاجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fay from the towns is allocated at God's direction to the Messenger, his close kin, orphans, the poor, and wayfarers; he takes the kin to be the Prophet's family, Banu Hashim.
rows.anchor: يعني أهل بيت رسول الله وقرابته وهم بنو هاشم

rows.speaker: علي بن الحسين
rows.claim: Ali ibn al-Husayn says the close kin, orphans, poor, and wayfarers in the verse are their own kin, poor, and wayfarers.
rows.anchor: روى المنهال بن عمرو عن علي بن الحسين ع

rows.speaker: الفقهاء
rows.claim: All jurists take the orphans, poor, and wayfarers here to mean people generally; a similar position is also narrated from the Imams.
rows.anchor: وقال جميع الفقهاء هم يتامى الناس عامة وكذلك المساكين وأبناء السبيل وقد روي أيضا ذلك عنهم

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abu Jaʿfar transmits his father's view that the Prophet's and kin's shares belong to them, while they share with everyone in the remainder.
rows.anchor: وروى محمد بن مسلم عن أبي جعفر ع أنه قال: كان أبي يقول لنا سهم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وسهم ذي القربى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent wording gives the kin their share whether wealthy or poor, which is the Shafiʿi position.
rows.anchor: والظاهر يقتضى أن ذلك لهم سواء كانوا أغنياء أو فقراء وهو مذهب الشافعي

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view assigns Fay to the poor among the Prophet's relatives, Banu Hashim and Banu al-Muttalib.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن مال الفيء للفقراء من قرابة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهم بنو هاشم وبنو المطلب

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Abu Abd Allah says their family has obligatory obedience and rights to anfal and the Prophet's selected valuables, such as exceptional mounts, fine slave women, and unique precious objects.
rows.anchor: وروي عن الصادق ع أنه قال: نحن قوم فرض الله طاعتنا ولنا الأنفال ولنا صفو المال

words: كَيْ لَا يَكُونَ دُولَةًۢ بَيْنَ ٱلْأَغْنِيَآءِ مِنكُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dawla is something passed around; this distribution prevents Fay from circulating among leaders as it did in pre-Islamic custom.
rows.anchor: والدولة اسم للشيء الذي يتداوله القوم بينهم يكون لهذا مرة ولهذا مرة أي لئلا يكون الفيء متداولا بين الرؤساء

words: كَيْ لَا يَكُونَ دُولَةًۢ بَيْنَ ٱلْأَغْنِيَآءِ مِنكُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address is to believers, excluding the Prophet and his household.
rows.anchor: وهذا خطاب للمؤمنين دون الرسول وأهل بيته ع

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says it was revealed after Muslim leaders asked the Prophet to take his chosen share and a quarter, leaving them the rest as in pre-Islamic practice; the Companions accepted God's command.
rows.anchor: قال الكلبي: نزلت في رؤساء المسلمين قالوا له يا رسول الله خذ صفيك والربع ودعنا والباقي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited poem lists the customary shares of booty: the leader's quarter, choice spoils, judgment, incidental booty, and surplus.
rows.anchor: وأنشدوا: لك المرباع منها والصفايا وحكمك والنشيطة والفضول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Accept and be content with what the Messenger gives from Fay; carry out his commands and avoid his prohibitions, since he commands and forbids only by God's command.
rows.anchor: أي ما أعطاكم الرسول من الفيء فخذوه وارضوا به وما أمركم به فافعلوه وما نهاكم عنه فانتهوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though revealed about Fay, the command applies generally to everything the Prophet enjoins or forbids.
rows.anchor: وهذا عام في كل ما أمر به النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ونهى عنه وإن نزل في آية الفيء

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Abu Abd Allah says God gave Muhammad all that He gave the other prophets: Solomon was told to give or withhold without account, while Muhammad received this command.
rows.anchor: وروى زيد الشحام عن أبي عبد الله ع قال: ما أعطى الله نبيا من الأنبياء شيئا إلا وقد أعطى محمدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fearing God here means leaving sins and fulfilling obligations; He severely punishes those who disobey and neglect His commands.
rows.anchor: في ترك المعاصي وفعل الواجبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse indicates that governing the community belongs to the Prophet and the Imams who succeed him; examples include his varied rulings over Khaybar, Banu Nadir, Banu Qaynuqa, Banu Qurayza, and Mecca.
rows.anchor: وفي هذه الآية إشارة إلى أن تدبير الأمة إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وإلى الأئمة القائمين مقامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poor emigrants are those who migrated from Mecca to Medina and from the abode of war to the abode of Islam, expelled from their homes and possessions.
rows.anchor: الذين هاجروا من مكة إلى المدينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They seek God's grace and approval and support God's religion; God calls them truthful and highly honored.
rows.anchor: فضلا من الله ورضوانا وينصرون الله

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the verse identifies the deserving poor as emigrants expelled from their homes and property.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج: بين سبحانه من المساكين الذين لهم الحق فقال للفقراء المهاجرين الذين أخرجوا من ديارهم

words: وَٱلَّذِينَ تَبَوَّءُو ٱلدَّارَ وَٱلْإِيمَٰنَ مِن قَبْلِهِمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Ansar settled in Medina, the abode of the Hijra, before the emigrants; the wording's estimate is that they settled the abode and embraced faith before them.
rows.anchor: يعني المدينة وهي دار الهجرة تبوأها الأنصار قبل المهاجرين وتقدير الآية والذين تبوؤوا الدار من قبلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faith is coordinated with abode in wording, not sense, because faith is not a place one can settle; the intended sense is that they chose faith.
rows.anchor: وعطف الإيمان على الدار في الظاهر لا في المعنى لأن الإيمان ليس بمكان يتبوؤوأ لتقدير وآثروا الإيمان

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One interpretation takes before them to mean before the emigrants arrived in Medina.
rows.anchor: من قبل قدوم المهاجرين عليهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes it as before the emigrants believed and identifies the group as the seventy men at Aqaba who pledged to fight all peoples.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه قبل إيمان المهاجرين والمراد به أصحاب ليلة العقبة وهم سبعون رجلا بايعوا رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Ansar loved the emigrants because they welcomed them into their homes and shared their property with them.
rows.anchor: لأنهم أحسنوا إلى المهاجرين وأسكنوهم دورهم وأشركوهم في أموالهم

words: وَلَا يَجِدُونَ فِى صُدُورِهِمْ حَاجَةًۭ مِّمَّآ أُوتُوا۟
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They felt no envy, resentment, or anger about the Banu Nadir wealth given to the emigrants instead of to them.
rows.anchor: أي لا يجدون في قلوبهم حسدا وحزازة وغيظا مما أعطي المهاجرون دونهم من مال بني النضير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They preferred the emigrants, putting them ahead of themselves in their wealth and homes, even though they themselves were in need; this makes their reward greater.
rows.anchor: ويؤثرون المهاجرين ويقدمونهم على أنفسهم

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: Anas ibn Malik reportedly swore that there were no misers among the Ansar and recited this verse.
rows.anchor: ويروى أن أنس بن مالك كان يحلف بالله تعالى ما في الأنصار بخيل ويقرأ هذه الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To be protected from the soul's avarice is to be kept from its miserliness; such people succeed and win God's reward and Paradise.
rows.anchor: ومن يدفع عنه ويمنع عنه بخل نفسه

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says one is spared avarice by not taking what God forbids and not withholding what God commands one to give.
rows.anchor: وقيل: من لم يأخذ شيئا نهاه الله عنه

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr identifies avarice as taking unlawful wealth and withholding alms.
rows.anchor: وقيل: شح النفس هو أخذ الحرام ومنع الزكاة عن سعيد بن جبير

rows.speaker: الحديث
rows.claim: A hadith says avarice does not coexist with faith in a Muslim's heart, nor dust from God's path with Hell's smoke in his body.
rows.anchor: لا يجتمع الشح والإيمان في قلب رجل مسلم ولا يجتمع غبار في سبيل الله ودخان جهنم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One parsing makes the Ansar an initial subject whose predicate is that they love the emigrants; the Prophet gave them little of the Fay, with reports differing between two and three men.
rows.anchor: أحدهما: أنه رفع على الابتداء وخبره يحبون من هاجر إليهم إلى آخره لأن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لم يقسم لهم شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the phrase is genitive, coordinated with the poor emigrants, and the following description of the Ansar is a circumstantial clause.
rows.anchor: والآخر: أنه في موضع جر عطفا على الفقراء المهاجرين وعلى هذا فيكون قوله يحبون من هاجر إليهم

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan says the later arrivals are all who follow the emigrants and Ansar until the Day of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: يعني من بعد المهاجرين والأنصار وهم جميع التابعين لهم إلى يوم القيامة عن الحسن

rows.speaker: الأصم وأبو مسلم
rows.claim: Al-Asamm and Abu Muslim identify them as everyone who became Muslim after the Hijra ended and after the Ansar's faith.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هم كل من أسلم بعد انقطاع الهجرة وبعد إيمان الأنصار عن الأصم وأبي مسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent sense is those who succeeded the earlier groups; after them may also refer to rank and merit.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن المراد والذين خلفوهم ويجوز أن يكون المراد من بعدهم في الفضل

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view explains God's transcendence and majesty as being above the attributes of created things and all that does not befit Him.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو المتعالي عن صفات المحدثين المتعظم عما لا يليق به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Glory be to God above what idolaters associate with Him, including idols and anything else.
rows.anchor: أي تنزيها له عما يشرك به المشركون من الأصنام وغيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Khaliq means the creator of bodies and their accidents.
rows.anchor: للأجسام والأعراض المخصوصة. وقيل: المقدر للأشياء

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation calls God the determiner of things by wisdom who brings them into existence by His will.
rows.anchor: وقيل: المقدر للأشياء بحكمته المحدث للأشياء على إرادته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Bariʾ is the one who originates creation and makes bodies and accidents.
rows.anchor: المنشئ للخلق الفاعل للأجسام والأعراض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Musawwir shapes bodies in their diverse forms, such as animals and inanimate things.
rows.anchor: الذي صور الأجسام على اختلافها مثل الحيوان والجماد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The beautiful names include Allah, the Merciful, the Compassionate, the Powerful, the Knowing, and the Living; the commentary discussed this in al-Aʿraf.
rows.anchor: نحو الله الرحمن الرحيم القادر العالم الحي وقد مر بيانه في سورة الأعراف

words: يُسَبِّحُ لَهُۥ مَا فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All things glorify God: living beings verbally declare His transcendence, while inanimate things indicate it.
rows.anchor: أي ينزهه جميع الأشياء فالحي يصفه بالتنزيه والجماد يدل على تنزيهه

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet says God's greatest name occurs in six verses at the end of Surat al-Hashr.
rows.anchor: قال رسول صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asfar means books; the word derives from revealing meaning, as when a man uncovers his turban, a woman uncovers her face, or dawn brightens.
rows.anchor: الأسفار الكتب واحدها سفر وإنما سمي بذلك لأنه يكشف عن المعنى بإظهاره

words: وَإِن كَانُوا۟ مِن قَبْلُ لَفِى ضَلَٰلٍۢ مُّبِينٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In this clause inna is the lightened form of inna; the separating lām is required in kana's predicate to distinguish it from negative in.
rows.anchor: إن هذه مخففة من إن ولهذا لزمها اللام الفارقة في خبر كان لئلا يلتبس بإن النافية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wa-akharina can be genitive, modifying an omitted noun coordinated with the unlettered, or accusative, coordinated with the pronoun in teaches them.
rows.anchor: وآخرين مجرورة لأنه صفة محذوف معطوف على الأميين أي وفي قوم آخرين ويحتمل أن يكون منصوبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase carrying books is an accusative circumstantial clause.
rows.anchor: في موضع النصب على الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One parsing supplies the censured comparison, making those who denied God's signs genitive; another supplies a deleted noun, making them the nominative object of blame.
rows.anchor: محذوف تقديره بئس مثل القوم الذين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everything in the heavens and earth glorifies God and attests to His oneness and lordship through signs of wise craftsmanship, proving His perfect attributes and that nothing resembles Him.
rows.anchor: أي ينزهه سبحانه كل شيء ويشهد له بالوحدانية والربوبية بما ركب فيها من بدائع الحكمة وعجائب الصنعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The past form sabbaha alongside the present yusabbihu signals God's continual glorification in past and future.
rows.anchor: وإنما قال مرة سبح ومرة يسبح إشارة إلى دوام تنزيهه في الماضي والمستقبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Malik can dispose of things; al-Quddus is worthy of reverence and free of defect; al-Aziz cannot be resisted; al-Hakim puts things in their proper place.
rows.anchor: أي القادر على تصريف الأشياء

rows.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
rows.claim: Mujahid and Qatada identify the unlettered people as the Arabs, who neither wrote nor read and had no prophet sent to them.
rows.anchor: يعني العرب وكانت أمة أمية لا تكتب ولا تقرأ ولم يبعث إليهم نبي عن مجاهد وقتادة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view identifies them as the people of Mecca, since Mecca is called the Mother of Cities.
rows.anchor: وقيل: يعني أهل مكة لان مكة تسمى أم القرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messenger is Muhammad, whose lineage and human kind are their own, as in the verse describing a messenger from among yourselves.
rows.anchor: يعني محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم نسبه نسبهم وهو من جنسهم كما قال لقد جاءكم رسول من أنفسكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sending an unlettered prophet fulfilled earlier prophets' scriptural predictions and blocks the suspicion that he borrowed his wisdom from books he read; his accurate accounts of past nations therefore show revelation.
rows.anchor: ووجه النعمة في أنه جعل النبوة في أمي موافقته لما تقدمت البشارة به في كتب الأنبياء السالفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He recites the Quran to them, containing the lawful and forbidden, proofs, and rulings.
rows.anchor: أي يقرأ عليهم القرآن المشتمل على الحلال والحرام والحجج والأحكام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He purifies them from unbelief and sins and calls them to what makes them pure.
rows.anchor: أي ويطهرهم من الكفر والذنوب ويدعوهم إلى ما يصيرون به أزكياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Book is the Quran and wisdom is the religious law.
rows.anchor: الكتاب القرآن والحكمة الشرائع

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view makes wisdom encompass the Quran, Sunna, and all divinely intended knowledge applied to what should be done or avoided in religion and worldly life.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن الحكمة تعم الكتاب والسنة وكل ما أراده الله تعالى فإن الحكمة هي العلم الذي يعمل عليه

words: وَإِن كَانُوا۟ مِن قَبْلُ لَفِى ضَلَٰلٍۢ مُّبِينٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before the Prophet was sent, they had plainly turned away from truth and religion.
rows.anchor: معناه وما كانوا من قبل بعثه إليهم إلا في عدول عن الحق وذهاب عن الدين بين ظاهر

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: Ata identifies the blast of the Trumpet as the first blast.
rows.anchor: وهي النفخة الأولى عن عطاء

rows.speaker: مقاتل والكلبي
rows.claim: Muqatil and al-Kalbi identify it as the final blast.
rows.anchor: والنفخة الأخيرة عن مقاتل والكلبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth and mountains are lifted from their places.
rows.anchor: أي رفعت من أماكنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are crushed once until everything on them is level, like stretched leather.
rows.anchor: أي كسرتا كسرة واحدة لا تثنى حتى يستوي ما عليها من شيء مثل الأديم الممدود

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another description has the earth and mountains crash into one another; mountains crumble and blow away, leaving one flat earth without peaks or hills.
rows.anchor: وقيل: ضرب بعضها ببعض حتى تفتت الجبال وسفتها الرياح وبقيت الأرض شيئا واحدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dual feminine form of crushed reflects treating the earth as one whole and the mountains as one mass.
rows.anchor: وإنما قال دكتا لأنه جعل الأرض جملة واحدة والجبال دكة واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inevitable event is the establishment of the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: أي قامت القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky parts and opens up; it becomes extremely weak as its structure deteriorates.
rows.anchor: أي شديدة الضعف بانتقاض بنيتها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view compares the sky, after its solidity, to wool in its looseness and weakness.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو أن السماء تنشق بعد صلابتها فتصير بمنزلة الصوف في الوهى والضعف

rows.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
rows.claim: Hasan and Qatada explain the sky's edges as its outer limits and sides; malak can be singular or plural, and when the sky weakens the angels are at its sides.
rows.anchor: أي على أطرافها ونواحيها عن الحسن وقتادة والملك اسم يقع على الواحد والجمع

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view has angels waiting at the sky's sides for the command to drive Hell's people to it and greet and honor Paradise's people.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن الملائكة يومئذ على جوانب السماء تنتظر ما يؤمر به في أهل النار

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says eight angels will carry God's Throne above the creatures.
rows.anchor: من الملائكة عن ابن زيد

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: A report from the Prophet says four angels carry it now and four more will reinforce them on Resurrection Day.
rows.anchor: إنهم اليوم أربعة فإذا كان يوم القيامة أيدهم بأربعة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the eight are rows of angels whose number is known only to God.
rows.anchor: وقيل: ثمانية صفوف من الملائكة لا يعلم عددهم إلا الله تعالى عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On Judgment Day all morally responsible people are exposed before God.
rows.anchor: يعني يوم القيامة تعرضون معاشر المكلفين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nothing hidden from you remains hidden: the phrase can mean a hidden person, a hidden deed, or the verbal noun of anything hidden.
rows.anchor: أي نفس خافية أو فعلة خافية

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود وقتادة
rows.claim: Ibn Masud and Qatada report three presentations of creation: two with excuses and disputes, then a third when records fly into the hands, right or left.
rows.anchor: وروي في الخبر عن ابن مسعود وقتادة أن الخلق يعرضون ثلاث عرضات اثنتان فيها معاذير وجدال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not expose creation to learn what He did not know; He knows all their deeds by His essence and exposes them so creation can see them.
rows.anchor: وليس يعرض الله الخلق ليعلم من حالهم ما لم يعلمه فإنه عز اسمه العالم لذاته يعلم جميع ما كان منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person given the book in the right calls the people at the gathering to come and read it, rejoicing because it contains only obedience and brings no shame.
rows.anchor: وإنما يقوله سرورا به لعلمه بأنه ليس فيه إلا الطاعات

rows.speaker: أهل اللغة
rows.claim: Linguists also explain haʾum as meaning take it.
rows.anchor: وأهل اللغة يقولون أن معنى هاؤم خذوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here I thought means I knew and was certain in worldly life that I would meet my account and be repaid for obedience and sin.
rows.anchor: أي علمت وأيقنت في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final h in kitabiya is for rhyme and is a pause-completion h.
rows.anchor: والهاء لنظم رؤوس الآي وهي هاء الاستراحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He enjoys a life whose state pleases him because he receives reward and is safe from punishment.
rows.anchor: أي في حالة من العيش راضية يرضاها بأن لقي الثواب وآمن العقاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The garden is lofty in rank and location.
rows.anchor: أي رفيعة القدر والمكان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its fruits are near the one who reaches for them.
rows.anchor: أي ثمارها قريبة ممن يتناولها

rows.speaker: البراء بن عازب
rows.claim: Al-Bara ibn Azib says a person can take a fruit while asleep.
rows.anchor: قال البراء بن عازب: يتناول الرجل من الثمرة وهو نائم

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: Salman transmits from the Prophet that entry to Paradise comes with a divine pass naming its recipient and commanding admission to a lofty garden with near fruits.
rows.anchor: عن سلمان قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says nothing prevents their hands from reaching the fruit, and there are no thorns.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه لا يرد أيديهم عن ثمرها بعد ولا شوك عن قتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are told to eat and drink in Paradise.
rows.anchor: أي يقال لهم كلوا واشربوا في الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are congratulated for the righteous deeds they sent ahead during worldly life; the food is harmless and needs no excretion.
rows.anchor: أي قدمتم من أعمالكم الصالحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hanian means it causes no harm, so it requires no elimination through stool or urine.
rows.anchor: أنه ليس فيه ما يؤذي فلا يحتاج فيه إلى إخراج

rows.speaker: أهل المدينة
rows.claim: The people of Medina read the idol's name Wadd with a damma; other readers use a fatha.
rows.anchor: قرأ أهل المدينة ودا بالضم والباقون بالفتح

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abu Amr reads mimma khatayahum with yāʾ; the other readers have khatiʾatihim with tāʾ, lengthening, and hamza.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو مما خطاياهم والباقون مما خطيئاتهم بالتاء والمد والهمزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commentary says it discussed the variant in waladuhu in Surat Maryam.
rows.anchor: وقد ذكرنا الاختلاف في ولده في سورة مريم ع

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda says Wadd was an idol of the Kalb tribe and gives its name with a fatha; the cited verse supports that vocalization.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة: زعموا أن ودا كان صنم لهذا الحي من كلب وحكاه بالفتح

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن
rows.claim: Abu al-Hasan says Medina's damma may be a dialect form of the idol's name; his cited line has a damma.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو الحسن: ضم أهل المدينة الواو وعسى أن يكون لغة في اسم الصنم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fijaj are broad, divergent roads; alternatively, a fajj is a pass between two mountains.
rows.anchor: اللغة: الفجاج الطرق المتسعة المتفرقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Suwa is an idol here; elsewhere saʿa refers to a portion of the night, with sawʾa as a related form.
rows.anchor: والسواع هنا صنم وفي غيره الساعة من الليل ومثله السعواء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kibara means very great, following a scale from kabir to kubar to kibar, comparable to other intensive forms.
rows.anchor: والكبار الكبير جدا يقال: كبير ثم كبار ثم كبار ومثله عجيب وعجاب وعجاب

rows.speaker: أعرابي
rows.claim: A Bedouin heard the Prophet recite makran kibara and exclaimed that his Lord was eloquent; al-Tabrisi calls this Bedouin rudeness because God is not described as eloquent.
rows.anchor: وروي أن أعرابيا سمع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقرأ ومكروا مكرا كبارا فقال ما أفصح ربك يا محمد

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj derives diyar from dawran, with the original form's waw turned into yāʾ and assimilated; ma bi-d-dar diyar means nobody is there moving about.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج يقال ما بالدار ديار أي ما بها أحد يدور في الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A poet's line uses the connected diyar where separated wording would ordinarily be expected, for poetic necessity.
rows.anchor: فجعل المتصل موضع المنفصل ضرورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tibaqan is accusative either by supplying created them layered or as an adjective describing the seven heavens as layered.
rows.anchor: طباقا منصوبا على أحد وجهين أن يكون على تقدير خلقهن طباقا وأن يكون نعتا لسبع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nabatan is an accusative verbal noun from an omitted verb, anbatakum fanabattum; al-Zajjaj says it follows the sense, since anbatakum means made you grow.
rows.anchor: نباتا مصدر فعل محذوف تقديره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ma in mimma khatiʾatihim is extra, strengthening the statement.
rows.anchor: وما من قوله { مما خطيئاتهم } مزيدة لتأكيد الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seven heavens are layered, one above another like domes.
rows.anchor: أي واحدة فوق الأخرى كالقباب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the moon lights the side of each heaven facing it and its face shines for people on earth, as does the sun.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال يضيء ظهره لما يليه من السماوات ويضيء وجهه لأهل الأرض وكذلك الشمس

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view takes in them to mean with them: the moon is made with the heavens as a light for earth's inhabitants.
rows.anchor: قيل فيه وجوه أحدها: أن المعنى وجعل القمر نورا في السماوات والأرض عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view takes in them as within their sphere, as one may say a well is in a group of houses though it lies in only one.
rows.anchor: كما تقول أتيت بني تميم وإنما أتيت بعضهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun is a lamp because it was made to illuminate earth's inhabitants, as a lamp illuminates a person.
rows.anchor: أي مصباحا يضيء لأهل الأرض لما كانت الشمس جعل فيها النور للاستضاءة به كانت سراجا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humanity's original creation began with Adam, who was made from earth, and all people descend from him.
rows.anchor: يعني مبتدأ خلق آدم وآدم خلق من الأرض والناس ولده

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation is that God originated everyone through nourishment from what the earth grows and what grows within it.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه أنه أنشأ جميع الخلق باغتذاء ما تنبته الأرض ونما فيها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further explanation describes growth from smallness to old age and from shortness to height.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه أنبتكم من الأرض بالكبر بعد الصغر وبالطول بعد القصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God returns people to earth as corpses and brings them out alive at resurrection; the verbal noun emphasizes the act of bringing out.
rows.anchor: منها عند البعث أحياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God spread the earth so people could walk and settle upon it.
rows.anchor: أي مبسوطة ليمكنكم المشي عليها والاستقرار فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth was spread so people could travel its broad paths.
rows.anchor: أي طرقا واسعة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says these are different routes, or paths across plains and passes through mountains.
rows.anchor: وقيل: سبلا في الصحارى وفجاجا في الجبال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These favors show that God alone deserves worship without association, knows people's interests, and wisely governs them; people should not answer His blessings with disbelief and denial.
rows.anchor: وإنما عدد سبحانه هذه الضروب من النعم امتنانا على خلقه وتنبيها لهم على استحقاقه للعبادة خالصة من كل شرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah says his people disobeyed what he ordered and forbade them.
rows.anchor: فيما أمرتهم به ونهيتهم عنه يعني قومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They followed their wealthy leaders, deluded by their possessions, and argued a true messenger would be rich.
rows.anchor: أي واتبعوا أغنياء قومهم اغترارا بما آتاهم الله من المال والولد فقالوا لو كان هذا رسولا لله

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says the poor and low-status people followed their chiefs, whose wealth and children brought only worldly ruin and punishment in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن معناه اتبع الفقراء والسفلة الرؤساء الذين لم يزدهم كثرة المال والأولاد إلا هلاكا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Walad is read with either a damma or fatha; walad may mean a group of children while walid means one, though another view treats both forms as equivalent.
rows.anchor: فالولد الجماعة من الأولاد والولد الواحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khasara means ruin through loss of capital; another explanation simply glosses it as destruction.
rows.anchor: الخسار الهلاك بذهاب رأس المال

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan explains their makr kabara as immense plotting.
rows.anchor: أي كبيرا عظيما عن الحسن

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the phrase means they uttered a great statement.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه قالوا قولا عظيما عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak explains their plotting as audacity against God and denial of His messengers.
rows.anchor: وقيل: اجترؤوا على الله وكذبوا رسله عن الضحاك

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says they incited their lower-status followers to kill Noah.
rows.anchor: وقيل: مكرهم تحريشهم سفلتهم على قتل نوح ع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The chiefs told the people not to stop worshipping their idols, then named particular famous idols after the general prohibition to exalt them.
rows.anchor: أي لا تتركوا عبادة أصنامكم ثم خصوا أصناما لهم معروفة بعد دخولها في الجملة الأولى تعظيما لها

words: وَدًّا وَلَا سُوَاعًا وَلَا يَغُوثَ وَيَعُوقَ وَنَسْرًا
rows.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Qatada say these were the names of idols worshipped by Noah's people and later by the Arabs.
rows.anchor: وهذه أسماء أصنام كانوا يعبدونها ثم عبدتها العرب فيما بعد عن ابن عباس وقتادة

words: وَدًّا وَلَا سُوَاعًا وَلَا يَغُوثَ وَيَعُوقَ وَنَسْرًا
rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn Kab says the names belonged to righteous people between Adam and Noah; Iblis urged later generations to make images of them, which eventually became idols of worship.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن هذه أسماء قوم صالحين كانوا بين آدم ونوح ع فنشأ قوم بعدهم يأخذون أخذهم

words: وَدًّا وَلَا سُوَاعًا وَلَا يَغُوثَ وَيَعُوقَ وَنَسْرًا
rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another account says Noah guarded Adam's body on a mountain in India; Iblis claimed to make a likeness for people to circumambulate, carved five idols, and led them to worship them.
rows.anchor: وقيل: كان نوح يحرس جسد آدم على جبل بالهند ويحول بينه وبين الكفار لئلا يطوفوا بقبره
